p:cNvPr.descr: PART 2: An image of the phosphoglycerate mutase reaction. At the top is 3-phosphoglycerate, where C bonds up to –OOC, left to H, and right to C, which bonds right to O, which bonds right to H. C also bonds down to H2C, which bonds right to O, which bonds right to PO3 with a minus 2 charge (in blue). A red arrow points from the bond line between O and H and points up to PO3 with a minus 2 charge (in pink), which bonds right to N+. A red arrow points from this bond line to N+. N+ is also the left point of a pentagon. The top point bonds up and right to His. The bottom right point is N over H. The top right and bottom left sides are double-bonded. Below this is another pentagon with double-bonded sides on the top left and right. At the bottom left point is HN. The bottom right point bonds down and right, then right to His. The top point is N, which has two red dots above and an arrow point left to the second H. Below this are reversible arrows. This is step 1: Phosphoryl transfer occurs between an active-site His and C-2(OH) of the substrate. A second active-site His acts as general base catalyst. Below this is 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate (2,3-BPG), which is a replica of the image above, but the first O bonds right to PO3 with a minus 2 charge (in pink). The top pentagon has a left point of N with two dots and an arrow points down to P. The top point of the second pentagon is H over N+. A red arrow points from the bond line between O and PO3 witha minus 2 charge to the H in H over N+. Below this are reversible arrows. This is step 2: Phosphoryl transfer from C-3 of the substrate to the first active-site His. The second active-site His acts as general acid catalyst. Below this 2-phosphoglycerate, which is the same as 3-phosphoglycerate, but the first O bonds right to a pink PO3 with a minus 2 charge, and the second O bonds right to H. The PO3 with a minus 2 charge is blue. There are no red arrows in this image.
